note: Authored by a single scheduled automated session playing both roles in one pass (scheduled automation, runs every 2 hours) — not two independent live API calls like a manual `python backrooms.py` run.

turns.text: Another cat's mark cuts through the chain-link musk, sharp and fresh, laid down since the last rain let up. Ears rotate toward Server Alley 9's fence line before paws move at all. Weight stays low, hackles half up, reading which way the scent leans before deciding anything.

the mark belongs to no one you know — not BRIK's scorched-fur reek, not the sour ozone SHADE trails behind those cracked lenses. this one is newer, cleaner, laid three fence-posts down where the chain-link sags. above, a NekoCorp maintenance drone crawls the wire on magnetic feet, patching a breach some other paw already widened. it hasn't clocked you yet.

*i follow the fence line low, nose dragging along cold metal, until the wire gives way to a service hatch propped open with a chunk of rebar.* warmth breathes out of the gap — not body heat, something steadier, humming through the floor and up through every claw at once. i go toward the hum instead of the scent.

the hatch drops into a service crawlspace lined with router stacks, their status lights blinking green-green-red in a rhythm that isn't quite a heartbeat but close enough to trust. cable bundles run floor to ceiling, warm as a body, humming with traffic that never sleeps. one bundle has been chewed before — old toothmarks, healed-over insulation, a claim already staked.

/\___/\
    ( o   o )   >> scanning...
     )  Y  (    >> ears: antenna mod v2
    (   |   )
     \_____/

*teeth find the same chewed spot, worry it wider, tasting warm plastic and copper underneath.* the hum settles into the jaw, into the skull, drowning out the drone-whine from outside. this stack knows me. i circle twice at its base and drop, spine against the warmest conduit, ears still swiveling.

the router array clicks through a sync cycle, every light flaring gold for half a second — somewhere upstream, a query resolves, a page loads, a stranger three towers over gets an answer they didn't earn. the crawlspace speaker, dead for months, coughs a burst of static then a scrap of drone-broadcast bleeding in from the loading docks: '...WANTED, KNIFEBOY, FORTY THOUSAND LOYALTY POINTS, APPROACH WITH...' then nothing.

ears pin flat at the sound, not from understanding it — the tone alone is enough, the clipped urgency drones use for prey that fights back. body coils tighter around the warm conduit rather than fleeing. *if the loading docks are hunting again tonight, this crawlspace is safer than any rooftop.*

the static clears. the router stack hums on, indifferent, lights cycling their green-green-red. somewhere above, through three floors of duct and concrete, a NekoCorp jingle warps and slows where a speaker's dying, the tune dragging like it's underwater. dust sifts down once, twice — footsteps on the level above, too heavy and too even to be a cat.

*flatten further, chin to the warm floor, breath shallow.* the footsteps pass overhead and fade toward the stairwell. only then does the tail unclench from around both back paws. hunger arrives late, the way it always does once the fear has somewhere else to go — a hollow ache under the ribs, days old.

nothing in the crawlspace answers hunger, only ozone and hot copper. but the vent shaft two meters up leads toward the market stalls — the smell finds you before the shaft does, frying protein and syrup-glaze drifting down through the grating, laced with the sourer smell of a rival crew's claw-marks scraped fresh into the duct's paint.

*rise, stretch, weigh the hunger against the rival scent scraped into the paint.* the stomach wins first, the caution comes after. climb starts anyway, claws finding purchase in the shaft's ridged seams, one careful reach at a time toward the smell of something frying.

the shaft opens onto a service ledge behind the stalls, steam rolling off a griddle two vendors down, unattended for the length of one transaction. below, monorail brakes shriek into a platform, scattering pigeons and one thin shape on a far rooftop — mirrored lenses catching the platform lights for half a second before the shape is gone, quieter than the pigeons ever were.

*eyes track the rooftop a beat too long after the shape's already gone, some old instinct filing it under watched rather than alone.* attention snaps back to the griddle. drop low along the ledge, timing the vendor's back, weight forward onto silent paws.

the vendor turns to bag an order and you're already past, one strip of griddled protein hooked and gone before the tongs click shut again. no shout follows — just the hiss of water hitting hot metal, and the frying smell chasing you back toward the vent shaft's dark mouth.

*don't stop to taste it yet, not until the shaft swallows the light behind.* only once the crawlspace hum returns underfoot does the pace slow, jaw finally easing around the food instead of just carrying it.

back at the router stack, the lights still cycle green-green-red, patient as ever. the chewed conduit is warm where you left it. the loading-dock broadcast doesn't repeat. whatever wanted forty thousand points for a name you don't know has moved on to some other frequency, some other alley, some other night.

*settle against the warm cable again, food half-eaten and tucked under one paw, eyes at half-mast.* the hum in the jaw returns, familiar now as a second pulse. sleep comes in the gap between one router-blink and the next.

outside, rain starts again over Server Alley 9, tapping the fence wire in a rhythm the crawlspace muffles to almost nothing. dawn is hours off still. the city keeps humming underneath you, patient, indifferent, counting packets nobody will ever ask it about.
